# GRISTORA marketing website — content consistency audit

**Date:** 15 November 2026  
**Scope:** Public routes generated by `marketing-site/`  
**Status:** Source review completed for the public route templates and core commercial journeys; final generated-site and browser acceptance remains W12.

## 1. Audit scope

Reviewed the public route templates for:
- Homepage and primary/secondary audience positioning.
- Professional Breweries and Homebrewers landing pages.
- Product feature index and generated feature-detail template.
- How It Works and Technical Principles.
- FAQ.
- Pricing, comparison and plan configurator.
- 404, robots and sitemap route generation.

The feature detail pages are generated from the shared `src/data/features.ts` catalogue; the catalogue remains read-only for this assignment.

## 2. Consistency baseline

The following statements are the approved public-content baseline:
- GRISTORA is brewing software in development; it is not currently available as a production service.
- Professional Breweries is the primary commercial audience; Homebrewers is a separate secondary audience.
- The public website is marketing and product-direction information, not the product application.
- The Home plan is one user; the Professional Brewery plan starts at five seats and increases in groups of five through 20.
- A three-month Home trial and one-month Brewery trial are proposed, not activated offers.
- Annual / two-year / three-year discounts of 15% / 25% / 35% are proposed terms, not final commercial approval.
- Monetary prices, currency, taxes, invoicing entity and contractual terms remain unpublished.
- The plan wizard is a configuration preview only. It does not create an account, activate a trial, collect card details, charge a payment or submit a sales request.
- More than 20 seats leads to custom-quote guidance. It is not a live lead form; a public sales email is still an owner input.
- Product capabilities and integrations must be described as planned or under consideration according to their source stages. Never imply that a roadmap item is released.
- GRISTORA is not a general ERP; excluded areas include sales, orders, distribution/shipping, keg tracking, CRM and accounting.

## 3. Route-level review

| Route family | Review focus | Result / required treatment |
|---|---|---|
| `/` | Business-first positioning, Homebrew secondary path, product maturity | Core positioning and development disclosure present. Keep primary CTA directed to Professional Breweries. |
| `/breweries/` | Planned workflow vs live production capability | Page explicitly says GRISTORA is in development and describes planned workflow. Maintain “planned” language for scheduling, quality and traceability. |
| `/homebrewers/` | Distinct Home path and availability | Keep separate from Business positioning; do not imply live calculators or an activated trial. |
| `/features/` and `/features/:slug/` | Roadmap stages and feature claims | Generated from shared catalogue; detail template identifies the product roadmap and states GRISTORA is in development. Stage language must remain visible. |
| `/how-it-works/` | Conceptual workflow vs functioning product | Use explanatory / planned wording; never present process diagrams as a currently operating service. |
| `/technical-principles/` | Methods, defaults, validation and limitations | Technical explanations must not be read as a promise of a released calculator or validated production result. |
| `/faq/` | Product maturity, integrations, pricing and trials | FAQ clearly states no production access, signup, trial activation or live payment. Commercial answer identifies all term discounts and trials as proposed. |
| `/pricing/` | Plans, terms, discounts, price publication and preview | Keep monetary prices unpublished until owner approval. Make proposed discounts and no-live-checkout disclosure prominent. |
| `/compare/` | Home vs Brewery scope and feature stage | Stage legend and comparison links are in place. Ensure all matrix entries derive from the feature catalogue. |
| `/get-started/` | Wizard, seat bands, trial, 20+ seats and payment | Wizard is a non-live preview; 20+ is guidance only. Do not add an invented contact address or imply request submission. |
| `/404` | Recovery paths | Provides routes back to Home, Breweries and Homebrewers. |
| `/robots.txt`, `/sitemap.xml` | Preview indexing and public route inventory | Preview is disallowed/noindex; sitemap is generated from the static route list and feature catalogue. Re-verify against the final generated output in W12. |

## 4. Cross-route consistency checks

- Business-first positioning is consistent with the homepage audience order and the dedicated Breweries page.
- The pricing FAQ and wizard use the same proposed Home/Brewery trial durations and discount ladder.
- The pricing journey distinguishes plan selection from a live commercial transaction.
- The 20+ seat path is explanatory only; no sales email or submission endpoint is invented.
- Product maturity is explicit on the homepage, audience pages, FAQ and feature detail template.
- Product scope exclusions are stated in FAQ and must remain consistent with all feature copy.
- The site uses English as its current public language; this audit does not authorize additional locales.
- The Pages preview remains noindex and is not a production launch.

## 5. Items to re-check in W12

1. Crawl the generated `dist/` output and validate every internal href/src target, including every generated feature detail route.
2. Compare all generated feature-detail titles, descriptions, canonical URLs and sitemap entries against the catalogue.
3. Verify the pricing, comparison and wizard copy together in desktop and mobile browser screenshots.
4. Search generated HTML for unqualified claims such as “available”, “start your trial”, “sign up”, “buy now”, “integrates” and “predicts”; review each occurrence in context.
5. Verify no external form action, payment endpoint, analytics script, cookie or tracking request has been introduced.
6. Check 320px, 390px, 768px, 1024px and 1440px widths, keyboard navigation, focus visibility, screen-reader labels and 200% zoom.
7. Confirm the final Pages preview remains noindex and production domain/DNS/Vercel remain untouched.

## 6. Owner-dependent launch inputs

This audit does not resolve the owner-dependent items recorded in the website follow-through plan: monetary prices, currency/tax/invoicing, approved discounts, contract and renewal terms, trial eligibility/activation/card requirement, sales contact for 20+ seats, privacy/legal text and actual registration/billing destination.

## 7. Scope and conclusion

No product code, product catalogue, product task queue, payment flow, account provisioning or analytics implementation was changed. This is a content-control review, not a legal review or a production-launch approval. The remaining generated-output and browser checks are assigned to W12.
